title: Laid Off 2 Days Before Christmas, Now He Makes $60k/Month Reselling
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
promo_conflict: The guest offers to find auction deals for listeners and invites them to call or text him (L0763-L0789); no paid sponsor conflict is disclosed.

stated_problem.quote: I'm never going to work for someone else that can control my income like that.

idea.name: Reselling liquidation and auction goods
idea.one_liner: Buy returned, surplus, or auction goods and resell them through a local store, social media, and marketplaces.
idea.customer: Local shoppers and online buyers seeking discounted goods; some buyers are businesses.
idea.offer: Mixed returned and auction goods including furniture, appliances, clothes, tools, and other items.
idea.revenue_model: Buy goods below resale value and earn the difference on retail or marketplace sales.

key_quotes.quote: I did $60,000 in sales
Don't go into debt to learn how to sell because it's not the buying, it's the selling.

claims.claim: He reports $60,000 in sales in his first month.
claims.quote: I did $60,000 in sales

claims.claim: The host says the guest claimed $60,000 in first-month revenue, half of it profit.
claims.quote: he claims to have made $60,000 his first month with half of that being profit reselling random things in middle of nowhere rural Washington.

claims.claim: He began with a $1,200 purchase and reinvested the profit.

claims.quote: What did you sell them for each? >> 50 bucks.

claims.claim: He says he paid $228 for an item.
claims.quote: I paid $228 for something like that.

claims.claim: The host calculates a 25x return on the item.
claims.quote: So 25x on your money. Start with something you already own.

claims.claim: A Saturday furniture sale made about $3,000.
claims.quote: we ended up selling all this stuff and made about $3,000 that Saturday

claims.quote: we probably had probably had 30 or 40 people come down to the sale.

claims.quote: our biggest day of the year. We did $15,000 in sales.

Sold from a storefront and attracted drive-by shoppers with items displayed outside.

idea.name: Reselling used restaurant equipment
idea.one_liner: Source surplus and used restaurant equipment and resell it to restaurant operators through marketplaces and referrals.
idea.customer: Restaurants and restaurant owners needing working equipment.
idea.offer: Used restaurant equipment, including items acquired from former restaurant operations and auctions.
idea.revenue_model: Buy equipment below resale value and resell it at a markup; referrals from food-distributor salespeople generated leads.

key_quotes.quote: I did so well reselling restaurant equipment that I went on Gov deals and started buying more.

claims.claim: He offered food-distributor salespeople a 10% commission for leads.
claims.quote: So, I'd pay them 10% commission on any lead that they would give me.

claims.claim: He approached about 20 salespeople and ended up with three strong referral partners.
claims.quote: I probably only worked through about 20 and uh ended up with three really good ones.

acquisition_channels.details: He recruited US Foods and Cisco salespeople who already visited restaurant customers, offering commission for leads.

ideas.delivery: He stored and sometimes pressure-washed equipment, handled sales himself, and fulfilled equipment sales to restaurant buyers.
ideas.other_uk_rules: UK GDPR and PECR apply to customer databases and direct marketing. The Consumer Rights Act 2015 and product-safety requirements may apply to resale; commercial commission-agent arrangements can also have contractual and regulatory implications.

idea.customer: Homeowners replacing old or broken windows.
idea.revenue_model: Sell windows and installation at a markup over product and labor costs.
